method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of every prose passage, stepwise replay of all 15 encoded tableaux and their line references, exercise-count comparison, and exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Quantified tableau proof search, eigenvariable-rule ordering, three worked closed-tableau constructions, repeated use of unrestricted quantifier rules, branch closure and two exercise sets containing 9 signed-formula problems.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section introduces tableaux with quantifiers and advises applying rules governed by the eigenvariable condition early, because those applications will occur higher in the finished tableau.
samples.checks: The Marathi preserves the advice as a heuristic about inference order, retains the eigenvariable condition rather than turning it into a rule name, and keeps the finished-tableau qualification.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The first example tests existential-not-A implies not-universal-A by starting with the false-signed conditional. False conditional yields true existential-not-A and false not-universal-A. A fresh constant a instantiates the true existential; the two negation rules produce false A(a) and true universal-A, and universal instantiation with a closes the branch.
samples.checks: All five successive tableau states preserve truth signs, rule labels, line references, checked flags, the fresh-a choice and the final contradictory A(a) pair.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The second example starts with false existential C(x,b), true existential A-and-B, and true universal B-implies-C. The eigenvariable rule is applied first to the true existential, using fresh a because b already occurs. The remaining quantifier rules may reuse closed terms; choosing a, expanding the conjunction and then the conditional yields closure.
samples.checks: All five tableau states preserve the selected a instance, branch order, repeated-use policy for lines 1 and 3, conjunction products, conditional split and both closure witnesses. OLTAB-003 records the bounded clarification from any term to any closed term.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The third example begins with true universal A, true universal-A implies existential-B, and true not-existential-B. It first eliminates negation, delays non-eigenvariable quantifier rules and branching, then branches on the conditional. Fresh b and c are introduced on the two branches; reusing the suitable closed terms b and c in the universal and false-existential rules closes the branches respectively.
samples.checks: All five tableau states preserve the defer-order advice, the b/c freshness choices, left/right branch structure, exact rule applications and final closure pairs. OLTAB-003 records the closed-term clarification; OLTAB-004 corrects the narrative's false-existential reference from line 3 to its actual line 4.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The two problem sets ask for closed tableaux for six and three listed signed-formula collections respectively.
samples.checks: All 9 exercise items, their order, signs, variable names, parentheses, connectives and quantifier scopes are byte-preserved; only the repeated instruction was translated.

source_observations: OLTAB-003 documents two source passages whose unrestricted term-choice wording omits the standing closed-term requirement declared in OLP-0101.
The selected constants a, b and c are closed terms, so the clarification changes no displayed inference.
OLTAB-004 documents and corrects a narrative reference to line 3 where the derived false-existential formula and the final tree both require line 4.
The unit contains 15 oltableau environments and 9 exercise items in both source and target.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The eigenvariable, closed-term, tableau and signed-formula terminology remains open to expert correction where exact specialist Marathi evidence is sparse.
The tall tableau layouts will receive page-level visual inspection after the complete Tableaux chapter enters a cumulative reader.
